Set up Microsoft sign-in for database access

Source: R/backend__microsoft.R
oauth_db_microsoft_client.Rd

Create a Microsoft Entra sign-in client for database and platform access. Choose the services or token targets the app uses, then pass the client to shinyOAuth's UI and server modules.

Usage

oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "sql",
  tenant_id,
  client_id,
  redirect_uri,
  client_secret = NULL,
  ...,
  provider = shinyOAuth::oauth_provider_microsoft(tenant = tenant_id, id_token_validation
    = TRUE, userinfo_required = FALSE),
  token_targets = .odb_microsoft_targets(services),
  token_target_default = if (length(token_targets)) {
names(token_targets)[[1L]]
 }
    else {
     character()
 },
  scopes = .odb_microsoft_client_scopes(services, token_targets)
)

Arguments

services

One or more of "sql", "postgres", "fabric", "kql", "dax", "graphql", "onelake", or "databricks_entra". The first service selects the default token target.

tenant_id

Microsoft Entra tenant ID. Ignored when provider is supplied.

client_id

Application ID from the OAuth registration.

redirect_uri

Registered URL where the browser returns after sign-in.

client_secret

Client secret, or NULL for a public client.

...

Other arguments for shinyOAuth::oauth_client().

provider

Custom shinyOAuth provider, replacing the default.

token_targets

Named token targets, replacing the service defaults. Use list() for a client without named targets. In that case, default scopes come from services, which must select one resource. Supply scopes explicitly to replace those consent defaults.

token_target_default

Default target name, or character() for none.

scopes

OAuth scopes to request, replacing the defaults.

Value

A shinyOAuth OAuthClient. Create it outside server().

Details

The Entra registration needs delegated permissions for the selected services. Users also need access to the database or Fabric items. When PostgreSQL is combined with other services, its preset requests the delegated user_impersonation scope instead of .default.

Custom scopes, provider, and token_targets replace their defaults. An existing shinyOAuth client can be used in place of this preset. For a deployment-specific resource such as Oracle Database, supply custom token_targets; see vignette("oracle", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

See also

vignette("getting-started", package = "shinyOAuthDB") links to each source's setup. For custom permissions and targets, see vignette("getting-started", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Other sign-in configuration: oauth_db_bigquery_client(), oauth_db_databricks_client(), oauth_db_databricks_provider(), oauth_db_salesforce_client(), oauth_db_snowflake_client(), oauth_db_snowflake_provider(), oauth_db_supabase_client()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = c("fabric", "sql"),
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)
} # }
